intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle through the stunning Milford Sound fiord, exploring sea caves, waterfalls, and dramatic coastal cliffs. This guided kayaking experience puts you right at water level with views of Mitre Peak and lush rainforest. Wildlife encounters with dolphins, seals, and penguins are common. Perfect blend of light activity and breathtaking scenery for hikers who love coastal environments.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge on New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Operated by AJ Hackett, the pioneers of commercial bungee jumping, this is a bucket-list adrenaline experience. The gondola ride to the pod over the canyon is thrilling in itself. A must-do for adventure seekers visiting the South Island, conveniently based near Queenstown's lakefront.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Hike a section of the famous Abel Tasman Coast Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, winding through golden-sand beaches, turquoise bays, and native bush. The Torrent Bay to Bark Bay section is particularly stunning with beachfront camping spots and tidal crossings. Water taxis can drop you off and pick you up, making it flexible for day hikers. Combine hiking with swimming in pristine coastal waters.
experiences.location: Abel Tasman National Park, Tasman Bay

experiences.name: Queenstown Waterfront Dining Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a memorable dinner at one of Queenstown's iconic lakefront restaurants such as Rata or Botswana Butchery, showcasing New Zealand's finest local produce including South Island lamb, Central Otago pinot noir, and fresh seafood. Dine with panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. A perfect cultural and culinary reward after days of adventure activities.

experiences.name: Kaikoura Coastal Clifftop Walk & Whale Watch
experiences.description: Combine a scenic clifftop hike along the Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway with a world-class whale watching boat tour. The walkway hugs the dramatic coastline with seals basking on rocks below and views of the Seaward Kaikoura Ranges. The whale watching cruise offers close encounters with sperm whales, dolphins, and albatross. Kaikoura is one of the world's best marine wildlife destinations, blending hiking and ocean culture seamlessly.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$3 NZD) into Queenstown town center. Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Drop bags and take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront and Earnslaw Wharf to get your bearings. Enjoy free views of The Remarkables mountain range across Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown town center on foot. Visit the lively Queenstown Mall pedestrian area. Grab dinner at a budget-friendly spot and rest up after the flight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Fergburger (iconic Queenstown burger joint, ~$15–18 NZD) — arrive early afternoon to beat the queue
meals.dinner: Vudu Cafe & Larder or Rata Takeaways for affordable wraps and bowls (~$12–16 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Exchange currency or use ATMs in Queenstown CBD. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport (Skinny or 2degrees are cheapest). Download the Orbus app for cheap local bus travel.

day_by_day.morning: Early start: hike the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nuku). The trail starts a short walk from town and takes about 2–3 hours return. Stunning 360-degree panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to town and visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park entrance area, then walk along the lakefront. In the afternoon, take the free Frankton Track walk along the lake edge (~5 km one way) or rent a bike (~$25 NZD/half day) to explore further. Visit the Queenstown Gardens — free, beautiful rose gardens and disc golf course.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Queenstown Night Markets (if Monday, check schedule — usually Thursday). Browse the waterfront and enjoy the sunset over the lake from the pier.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats and fruit from Pak'nSave supermarket (~$3 NZD) — stock up on groceries today
meals.lunch: Picnic packed from supermarket at the Queenstown Gardens (~$5 NZD)
meals.dinner: Winnies Pizza on The Mall — budget slices available (~$10–14 NZD) or self-catered pasta at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Hill hike is free and one of the best views in the area. Wear layers — November weather can be warm but changeable. Pak'nSave on Gorge Road is the cheapest supermarket in Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: ADVENTURE DAY: Nevis Bungy Jump — the highlight of the trip! Book in advance online with AJ Hackett for the best price (~$275 NZD). The Nevis is New Zealand's highest bungy at 134m. The shuttle departs from the AJ Hackett Station on Camp Street in Queenstown. The experience including transport takes approximately half a day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-bungy adrenaline recovery — head to the Shotover River area. Walk the free Arthurs Point track along the Shotover River gorge. Alternatively, relax at the Queenstown waterfront and celebrate your jump.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your Nevis Bungy jump! Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner tonight as a reward.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered eggs on toast at accommodation before the early shuttle (~$2 NZD)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pie from a bakery near the AJ Hackett station before or after (~$6–8 NZD). Try Vudu Cafe.
meals.dinner: Pub meal at Monty's or The World Bar — burger and chips deal (~$18–22 NZD). Check for happy hour specials.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nevis Bungy well in advance — it sells out fast, especially in summer (November). Wear comfortable clothes, no loose jewelry. Photos and video packages are available at extra cost (~$50–80 NZD) — worth considering as a one-time memory. AJ Hackett sometimes offers combo deals if you plan to do multiple jumps.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Glenorchy — take the Connectabus or drive the stunning 45-minute road along Lake Wakatipu (one of the most scenic drives in NZ). Arrive in the small village of Glenorchy. Start the Lagoon Pond Loop Walk (free, 1 hour easy) through wetlands with birdlife and mountain reflections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the start of the Routeburn Track — walk the first section of this world-famous Great Walk for free (no hut bookings needed for day walks). Walk to Routeburn Flats and back (~3–4 hours, 8 km return). Spectacular beech forest and mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via the scenic lakeside road. Stop at a lookout point for sunset photos over Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket eaten at the Routeburn Track start (~$5 NZD) — there are no food options in Glenorchy beyond a small cafe
meals.dinner: Self-catered stir fry or pasta at accommodation (~$5 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown to Glenorchy road is free to drive and widely considered one of the most beautiful in New Zealand. Fill up on petrol in Queenstown — there is no petrol station in Glenorchy. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. The Routeburn Track day walk is free and gives a taste of a Great Walk without the expensive hut fees.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Intercity or Naked Bus to Wanaka (~1.5 hours, ~$15–20 NZD). Check in to a Wanaka hostel (Base Wanaka or Wanaka Bakpaka, ~$30–35 NZD/night). Walk to the famous Wanaka Tree — the lone willow tree in Lake Wanaka that has become an iconic NZ photo spot. Free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mount Iron Track (1.5 hours return, free) — a prominent rocky hill right on the edge of Wanaka town offering 360-degree views of the lake, mountains, and surrounding farmland. One of the best easy hikes in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka town center. Visit the lakefront at sunset — Lake Wanaka at golden hour is stunning. Check out the Thursday Wanaka Farmers Market if available.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before bus departure
meals.lunch: Wanaka Bakery — famous pies and baked goods (~$6–8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Ritual Cafe or Kai Whakapai Cafe for affordable meals (~$15–18 NZD), or self-catered from New World supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a beautiful, slightly quieter alternative to Queenstown. Book bus tickets in advance for cheaper fares. Wanaka has a New World supermarket for grocery restocking. November is shoulder/early summer season — weather should be pleasant but pack a rain layer.

day_by_day.morning: Full day hike: Rob Roy Glacier Track in Mount Aspiring National Park (~4 hours return, 10 km, free). Drive or arrange a shuttle to the Raspberry Creek carpark (~45 min from Wanaka). The track crosses swing bridges over the Matukituki River and climbs through beech forest to a stunning glacial valley with waterfalls and views of the Rob Roy Glacier. One of the best day hikes in the South Island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Rob Roy hike or relax at the glacier viewpoint. Return to Wanaka in the afternoon. Cool down with a swim at Lake Wanaka beach (free).
day_by_day.evening: Relax in Wanaka. Visit Pemberton's Ice Cream for a budget treat (~$5 NZD). Watch the sunset over the lake.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the drive — the hike starts early
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the glacier viewpoint (~$5 NZD) — no food available at the track
meals.dinner: Relishes Cafe Wanaka for affordable dinner (~$16–20 NZD) or self-catered

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a car or shuttle to the Raspberry Creek carpark. Check with your hostel about shuttle options (~$20–25 NZD return) if you don't have a car. The track can be muddy — waterproof boots recommended. Start early to avoid afternoon heat and crowds. This is considered one of the top 10 day walks in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Morning walk along the Lake Wanaka Outlet Track to Albert Town (free, 1.5 hours one way). A flat, easy walk through wetlands and along the Clutha River outlet — great for birdwatching. Return by the same path or arrange a pickup.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Wanaka to Franz Josef Glacier on the West Coast (~4 hours drive or bus). Take the Intercity bus (~$35–45 NZD, book in advance). The journey crosses the Haast Pass — one of the most dramatic and scenic drives in New Zealand, through rainforest, waterfalls, and alpine passes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Franz Josef township. Check in to a budget hostel (Chateau Franz or Franz Josef YHA, ~$30–38 NZD/night). Explore the small village.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before bus departure
meals.lunch: Pack food for the bus journey — no food stops on this route
meals.dinner: Alice May Restaurant Franz Josef for affordable pub meals (~$18–22 NZD) or self-catered from the small local Four Square store (note: groceries are expensive on the West Coast — stock up in Wanaka)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass road (State Highway 6) is one of the great scenic drives of New Zealand. If on a bus, sit on the right side for the best views heading north. Stock up on groceries in Wanaka before leaving — West Coast towns are remote and expensive. Franz Josef is a tiny town so accommodation books out fast in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Walk — hike to the glacier terminal face viewpoint (free, ~2 hours return). The trail goes through the glacial valley with dramatic rock walls and braided rivers. Note: you cannot access the glacier ice itself without a guided tour, but the valley walk and viewpoint are spectacular and completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Alex Knob Track (6–8 hours return, free) for panoramic views of the glacier from above — start early if doing this full hike, or do the shorter Roberts Point Track (5–6 hours return). Alternatively, visit the free Lake Mapourika (8 km north of Franz Josef) — the largest lake on the West Coast with mirror-calm reflections of the surrounding rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in Franz Josef. The West Coast has spectacular sunsets — watch from the beach at Gillespies Beach if you have transport (~20 min drive).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the glacier valley walk
meals.dinner: Alice May Restaurant or self-catered at hostel

day_by_day.notes: Glacier heli-hike experiences (~$300–500 NZD) are available but beyond a tight budget. The free valley walk still offers incredible scenery. Sandflies are vicious on the West Coast — bring strong insect repellent (DEET-based). Weather on the West Coast is very changeable — check the MetService forecast each morning.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Franz Josef south to Te Anau (~5–6 hours by bus or car via Queenstown). Take the Intercity bus (~$45–55 NZD). Alternatively, travel back through Queenstown if needed. The journey passes through stunning West Coast and Fiordland scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check in to a budget hostel (Te Anau YHA or Barnyard Backpackers, ~$28–35 NZD/night). Walk the Te Anau lakefront (free) — Lake Te Anau is the South Island's largest lake.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small town of Te Anau. Visit the DOC Visitor Centre (free) to plan your Milford Sound day trip and get trail information. Watch the sunset over Lake Te Anau.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before bus departure
meals.lunch: Packed food for the bus journey
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies in Te Anau for budget pies and baked goods (~$6–10 NZD) or self-catered from the local supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is the base for Fiordland adventures. Stock up at the local supermarket (Four Square or Fresh Choice) for the next few days. Book the Milford Sound cruise in advance online for the best prices. The DOC Visitor Centre has excellent free maps and advice for all Fiordland walks.

day_by_day.morning: MILFORD SOUND DAY TRIP — one of the most iconic experiences in New Zealand. Take an early shuttle from Te Anau to Milford Sound (~2 hours, ~$35–45 NZD return via Go Orange or Tracknet). The drive itself through the Eglinton Valley and Homer Tunnel is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a budget Milford Sound cruise (~$50–65 NZD with Real Journeys or Go Orange — book online in advance for cheaper rates). The 2-hour cruise takes you past Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and through the fiord to the Tasman Sea. Seals, dolphins, and penguins are commonly spotted. After the cruise, walk the short Chasm Walk (~30 min, free) on the way back through the Homer Tunnel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by late afternoon/early evening. Debrief and share photos from the incredible day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered very early breakfast before the shuttle
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the cruise — bring your own food as the onboard cafe is expensive
meals.dinner: Sandfly Cafe Te Anau for affordable meals (~$14–18 NZD) or self-catered

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound is the single most visited attraction in New Zealand — book everything well in advance. The budget cruise option is just as scenic as premium options. Milford Sound gets 182 rain days per year — rain actually makes it more dramatic with hundreds of temporary waterfalls. Bring a waterproof jacket regardless of the forecast.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Kepler Track Day Walk — one of New Zealand's Great Walks, accessible for free as a day hike. Start at the Kepler Track Control Gates (15-min walk from Te Anau town). Hike to Brod Bay (~1.5 hours one way) through beautiful beech forest along the lake edge. Or continue further to the Luxmore Hut for bigger views (~5–6 hours return from Control Gates).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Kepler day hike or return to Te Anau. If back early, visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour (~$55 NZD, Real Journeys) — an underground cave system with glowworms, accessible only by boat. A more affordable alternative to Waitomo but still a budget consideration.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Te Anau. Pack bags for the journey back to Queenstown tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Kepler Track — eat at Brod Bay lakeside (~$5 NZD)
meals.dinner: Redcliff Cafe Te Anau for a slightly special dinner on this penultimate night (~$20–25 NZD) or self-catered

day_by_day.notes: The Kepler Track Great Walk hut system costs ~$65 NZD/night per hut — avoid these costs by day hiking only. The Control Gates are a 15-minute walk from Te Anau town center — no transport needed. November is an excellent time for this hike as the track is open and weather is generally good.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Te Anau back to Queenstown (~2 hours by bus or car, ~$25–35 NZD with Intercity or Tracknet). On the way, stop at the Mirror Lakes on the Milford Road (free) — perfectly still water reflecting the Earl Mountains. Also stop at Lake Gunn Nature Walk (~45 min loop, free) through ancient beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and Nevis Valley accommodation. Spend the afternoon doing any remaining activities or revisiting favourite spots. Consider the Kawarau Bridge Bungy (~$165 NZD) — the world's first commercial bungy site — if budget allows and you want another adrenaline hit. Or do the free Queenstown Hill walk again for a final view.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Queenstown. Explore the Queenstown Night Markets (Thursday markets on the waterfront — free entry, great atmosphere). Browse local craft stalls and enjoy street food.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before bus departure
meals.lunch: Packed food or stop at a cafe in Queenstown upon arrival (~$10–12 NZD)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food — budget $10–15 NZD for a full meal from various stalls. Try local lamb burgers, crepes, or Asian fusion options.

day_by_day.notes: The Mirror Lakes stop is a must on the Te Anau to Queenstown return journey — pull off the highway for a 10-minute walk to the viewing platform. The Thursday Night Markets in Queenstown are one of the best free evening activities in town. This is your last full day — soak up the atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Queenstown waterfront (free). If time allows before checkout, visit the free lookout at the top of Queenstown Hill for a final panoramic farewell view — or simply sit by the lake and reflect on the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation. Depending on your departure flight time, store luggage at the hostel or at the airport. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Queenstown Mall — look for budget options like postcards, local honey, or Whittaker's chocolate. Take the Orbus public bus to the airport (~$3 NZD).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Queenstown Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at accommodation — use up remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Fergburger one last time (~$15–18 NZD) — a fitting farewell to New Zealand
meals.dinner: Airport food or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport is small — arrive at least 90 minutes before departure. The Orbus Route 1 runs regularly to the airport. Use any remaining NZD on groceries, food, or small souvenirs before departure. Check airline baggage rules — NZ supermarkets sell great local products (Whittaker's chocolate, Pic's peanut butter, Manuka honey) that make excellent budget gifts.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival - Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear customs and collect luggage at Queenstown Airport. Transfer to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Queenstown's lakefront promenade to get oriented. Enjoy views of The Remarkables mountain range across Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown town center. Browse the lively waterfront area and get a feel for the local vibe. Early dinner and rest to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport or a nearby café such as Vudu Café & Larder on Rees Street — great coffee and cabinet food.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Fergburger, Queenstown's legendary burger institution — affordable, filling, and a local rite of passage. Expect a short queue but worth it.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Queenstown sits at altitude and jet lag can be significant on long-haul flights. Confirm boutique stay check-in time in advance. The drive from Queenstown Airport to the Nevis Valley area takes approximately 30–50 minutes depending on exact location — arrange a transfer or rental car ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head into central Queenstown for a scenic morning walk up the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Ben Lomond Reserve trailhead). The 2-hour return hike offers sweeping panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu, the town, and surrounding peaks — a perfect gentle introduction to South Island hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for lunch and to survey the landscape. Afterward, explore the Queenstown Gardens — a peaceful green peninsula jutting into the lake, ideal for a leisurely stroll and lawn bowls watching.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset drink at a lakefront bar. Head to 1876 Distillery & Bar or The Bunker for craft cocktails in a cozy atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or nearby — try The Grille at Hilton Queenstown for a buffet-style spread, or Bespoke Kitchen for healthy bowls and eggs.
meals.lunch: Skyline Restaurant at the top of the gondola — buffet with stunning views. Mid-range pricing and a great experience.
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — chef Josh Emett's celebrated New Zealand cuisine using local ingredients. Book ahead. Mid-range to slightly upscale but well worth it.

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown Hill walk is suitable for most fitness levels and takes 1.5–2 hours return. Wear layers as temperatures can shift quickly. The Skyline Gondola costs approximately NZD $40 per adult — check for combo deals with the luge if interested.

day_by_day.morning: NEVIS BUNGY JUMP — The headline adrenaline experience of the trip. Depart early from Queenstown to the Nevis Bungy base in the Nevis Valley. Transfer via off-road vehicle to the suspended cable car platform 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This is New Zealand's highest bungy jump, operated by AJ Hackett. The total experience including transfers takes approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown. Decompress and celebrate with a walk along the Queenstown Bay Beach. Optional: visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park on Brecon Street to see kiwi, tuatara, and native birds — a relaxed, educational afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at a Queenstown waterfront restaurant to mark the bungy milestone.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — pack energy foods like muesli, fruit, and coffee. The Nevis jump requires an early start.
meals.lunch: Light lunch back in Queenstown post-jump — try Habebe's for wraps and falafel, or Vudu Larder for fresh sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Queenstown Waterfront Dining Experience — dinner at Rata or Botswana Butchery on the lakefront. Enjoy a well-earned steak or fresh South Island salmon with lake views.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nevis Bungy Jump well in advance — it is one of the most popular activities in New Zealand and slots fill quickly, especially in November (peak summer season). Cost is approximately NZD $275 per person. Weight and health restrictions apply — check AJ Hackett's website. GoPro or professional photo/video packages available at extra cost.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (45 minutes from Queenstown along a stunning lakeside road). Begin the Routeburn Track day hike — tackle the section from Glenorchy to the Routeburn Flats and beyond toward Routeburn Falls (approximately 4–5 hours return). This is one of New Zealand's Great Walks with jaw-dropping alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Glenorchy for a late lunch. Explore the small, charming township and the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway — a flat, easy 30-minute loop through wetlands with excellent birdlife and mountain reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown along the lake road at golden hour — one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand. Relax at the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay or grab a packed lunch from a Queenstown deli before departure.
meals.lunch: Glenorchy Café — a beloved local institution serving hearty meals, homemade pies, and excellent coffee. Perfect post-hike refuel.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay area or back in Queenstown — try Minus 5° ICE BAR for a novelty experience, or keep it casual with a pizza at Winnie's on The Mall.

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track section to Routeburn Falls is approximately 8–10 km return and involves 300m of elevation gain. Suitable for moderately fit hikers. Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring rain gear — weather in the Dart River valley can change rapidly. No booking required for day hiking. Depart Queenstown by 8:00 AM to make the most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown toward Te Anau (2 hours). Stop at Kingston for a photo at the historic Kingston Flyer steam train site and views of the southern end of Lake Wakatipu. Continue to Te Anau — gateway to Fiordland National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Te Anau. Check in to mid-range accommodation (e.g., Te Anau Lodge or Distinction Te Anau Hotel). Explore the Te Anau lakefront and visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves (book in advance — a magical underground experience with a short boat ride through glowworm-lit caverns, 2 hours total).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Te Anau waterfront at dusk. The lake views toward the Fiordland mountains at sunset are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay before departing Queenstown.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a café in Mossburn or Te Anau township on arrival.
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — a local favorite serving Fiordland venison, lamb, and fresh fish in a cozy cottage setting. Mid-range pricing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Te Anau Glowworm Caves tours through Real Journeys well in advance. November is peak season. The drive from Queenstown to Te Anau is approximately 170 km and takes 2 hours — straightforward highway driving through beautiful pastoral scenery. This is a transition day to position for Milford Sound.

day_by_day.morning: MILFORD SOUND COASTAL KAYAKING — Depart Te Anau early for the 2-hour drive to Milford Sound along the iconic Milford Road (stop at Mirror Lakes and The Chasm along the way). Begin the Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking experience — paddle through the stunning fiord, exploring sea caves, waterfalls, and the dramatic coastline beneath Mitre Peak. Morning kayak sessions typically run 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, take a scenic Milford Sound cruise (1.5–2 hours) to see the fiord from a different perspective — spot fur seals, dolphins, and Stirling Falls up close. Return drive to Te Anau.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Te Anau. Relax, dry off, and enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Te Anau before departure — pack snacks and water for the kayaking session.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or the Milford Sound Lodge Café near the fiord — basic but convenient. Alternatively, bring your own food as options at Milford are limited and expensive.
meals.dinner: The Fat Duck Restaurant in Te Anau — excellent burgers, craft beer, and casual dining. Good value for a mid-range budget.

day_by_day.notes: Book Milford Sound kayaking with Rosco's Milford Kayaks or Go Orange well in advance — November slots fill fast. Guided kayak tours include all gear (wetsuit, paddle jacket, etc.). The Milford Road is one of the world's great scenic drives — allow extra time for photo stops. Weather at Milford Sound is famously unpredictable — rain actually enhances the experience with hundreds of temporary waterfalls cascading down the cliff faces.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike near Te Anau — tackle the Kepler Track day section from the Te Anau lakefront to Brod Bay (approximately 3 hours return, flat and beautiful through beech forest along the lake edge). A peaceful, restorative hike after the big Milford day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Te Anau toward Wanaka (2.5 hours via Queenstown or 3 hours via the Crown Range). Stop at Arrowtown en route — a charming historic gold-mining village with excellent cafés and a fascinating Chinese settlement museum. Stroll the tree-lined main street.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Wanaka. Check in to mid-range accommodation (e.g., Wanaka Homestead or Lakeside Apartments). Enjoy the relaxed Wanaka lakefront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Te Anau before departing.
meals.lunch: Arrowtown — lunch at Provisions of Arrowtown (excellent café with local produce) or The Fork & Tap for a casual pub lunch.
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen in Wanaka — beloved local restaurant with handmade pasta and wood-fired pizza. Book ahead. Mid-range pricing.

day_by_day.notes: The Kepler Track section to Brod Bay is flat and suitable for all fitness levels. The full Great Walk is 60 km but the day section is a gentle, beautiful introduction. Arrowtown is approximately 20 minutes from Queenstown — a worthwhile detour with excellent food and history. November sees the Arrowtown trees in full autumn-to-summer transition with beautiful foliage.

day_by_day.morning: Wanaka — hike the iconic Roys Peak Track. This 16 km return hike (1300m elevation gain, 5–6 hours) delivers one of the most photographed views in New Zealand — a ridgeline above Lake Wanaka with the Southern Alps as a backdrop. Start early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Roys Peak and cool down with a swim at Wanaka's town beach. Visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — a lone willow growing in the lake, one of New Zealand's most photographed landmarks.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Wanaka town. Browse the lakefront and enjoy a well-earned sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — Kika Wanaka or Ritual Café for excellent coffee and eggs.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the Roys Peak summit — there are no facilities on the trail. Sandwiches, trail mix, and plenty of water.
meals.dinner: Relishes Café in Wanaka — a long-standing local favorite with hearty, fresh New Zealand cuisine. Excellent value for mid-range budget.

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is closed from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season — by November 22 it should be fully open. Confirm current status closer to the date. The track is well-marked but steep — trekking poles are helpful. Start no later than 7:00–8:00 AM to complete comfortably and avoid afternoon heat. The summit viewpoint is at approximately 1578m.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Wanaka toward Kaikōura (approximately 5.5–6 hours via the Haast Pass and West Coast, or 4.5 hours via Christchurch — choose the scenic Haast Pass route for dramatic mountain and rainforest scenery). Depart early and stop at Haast Pass lookout and the Blue Pools Walk (30-minute return walk to turquoise glacier-fed pools).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north along the West Coast through Hokitika (optional stop at Hokitika Gorge — stunning turquoise water). Push on toward Christchurch or stop for the night at Greymouth/Hokitika if the drive is too long.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at overnight stop. If pushing through to Christchurch, check in and rest. If stopping on the West Coast, enjoy a quiet evening in Hokitika or Greymouth.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Wanaka before departure.
meals.lunch: Hokitika — lunch at Stumpers Bar & Café or pick up fresh whitebait fritters (a West Coast specialty) from a local takeaway.
meals.dinner: Christchurch — if you've made it through, try Lyttelton Road Bistro or Gatherings Restaurant for quality local cuisine. If on the West Coast, Hokitika's Café de Paris is a solid option.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — the Haast Pass route is approximately 450 km from Wanaka to Christchurch but is one of the most spectacular drives in New Zealand. Alternatively, consider splitting the journey and spending a night in Hokitika to reduce driving fatigue. The Blue Pools Walk near Makarora is highly recommended — only 30 minutes but visually stunning. Fill up with petrol before leaving Wanaka as stations are sparse on the West Coast.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Kaikōura (if not already there — 2.5 hours north of Christchurch). KAIKŌURA COASTAL CLIFFTOP WALK & WHALE WATCH — Begin the morning with the Kaikōura Peninsula Walkway, a spectacular 3-hour loop hike along dramatic clifftops above the Pacific Ocean. See fur seal colonies, dramatic coastal rock formations, and snow-capped Kaikōura Ranges as a backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: WHALE WATCHING — Join a Whale Watch Kaikōura boat tour (3.5 hours). Kaikōura is one of the world's best places to see sperm whales year-round, plus dolphins, albatross, and New Zealand fur seals. November is an excellent time with calm seas and abundant marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kaikōura township. The small town has a charming coastal character and excellent fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation or a Kaikōura café — The Store Kaikōura is a great local spot.
meals.lunch: Kaikōura's famous crayfish (rock lobster) from a roadside stall or The Crayfish Pot on the waterfront — a quintessential South Island experience. Budget NZD $30–50 for a half cray.
meals.dinner: Hislops Wholefoods Café or Nin's Bin (outdoor crayfish stall on the coastal road) for a memorable seafood dinner with ocean views.

day_by_day.notes: Book Whale Watch Kaikōura well in advance — it is one of New Zealand's most popular wildlife experiences. Cost is approximately NZD $175 per adult. Tours depart multiple times daily but November slots book out fast. The coastal walkway is free and requires no booking. Wear sun protection — the Kaikōura Peninsula is exposed. Kaikōura is approximately 2.5 hours north of Christchurch and 2 hours south of Nelson/Marlborough.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Kaikōura to the Abel Tasman National Park area via Blenheim and Nelson (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Stop in Blenheim for a quick visit to the Marlborough wine region — grab a tasting at a cellar door such as Cloudy Bay or Brancott Estate (open from 10:00 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: ABEL TASMAN COAST TRACK DAY HIKE — Arrive at Marahau (gateway to Abel Tasman). Take a water taxi into the park and hike a section of the famous Abel Tasman Coast Track — golden sand beaches, turquoise bays, and lush native bush. The Anchorage to Bark Bay section (approximately 12 km, 4 hours) is a highlight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marahau by water taxi. Check in to Nelson accommodation (e.g., Trailways Hotel Nelson or Mid City Motel). Enjoy a relaxed evening in Nelson.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Kaikōura before the drive.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the Abel Tasman hike — eat on one of the stunning golden sand beaches inside the park.
meals.dinner: Nelson — Hopgoods & Co. on Trafalgar Street is one of Nelson's finest restaurants with excellent local produce. Alternatively, try The Free House for craft beer and casual dining.

day_by_day.notes: Book Abel Tasman water taxis with Abel Tasman Sea Shuttles or Marahau Water Taxis in advance. Timetables are tide-dependent. The Abel Tasman Coast Track is one of New Zealand's Great Walks — no booking required for day hiking. Wear sunscreen and bring plenty of water. The beaches are stunning for swimming in November (water temperature around 18–20°C). Blenheim cellar doors are generally open 10:00 AM–4:30 PM — time the stop accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Nelson — New Zealand's sunniest city. Visit the Nelson Saturday Market (if applicable) or the World of Wearable Art & Classic Cars Museum (WOW Museum) — a unique and fascinating New Zealand institution. Stroll through the Nelson Arts Quarter and visit the stunning Christ Church Cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Queen Charlotte Drive from Havelock to Picton (1.5 hours, stopping at lookout points). Alternatively, explore the Pelorus River area for a swim in crystal-clear river pools (famously used in The Hobbit filming). Check in to Picton accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Picton's charming harbor. Visit the Edwin Fox Maritime Museum (the world's 9th oldest ship) and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of this gateway town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Nelson accommodation or a local café — try Penguino Café for excellent coffee and eggs.
meals.lunch: Havelock — 'The Greenshell Mussel Capital of the World.' Stop at Havelock Restaurant & Bar for a steaming pot of fresh mussels. Exceptional value and quality.
meals.dinner: Picton — Le Café on London Quay, a Picton institution with fresh seafood and harbor views. The green-lipped mussel chowder is exceptional.

day_by_day.notes: The WOW Museum in Nelson is open daily and costs approximately NZD $25 per adult — allow 1.5–2 hours. The Queen Charlotte Drive is narrow in places but manageable with care. Picton is the departure point for the Interislander ferry to Wellington (North Island) if extending the trip. November weather in the Marlborough Sounds area is typically warm and settled — ideal for coastal exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the South Island. If flying from Christchurch or Queenstown, begin the drive early. If time permits, take a final walk along the Queen Charlotte Track (Picton section — 1–2 hours return from the town wharf along the stunning Marlborough Sounds). A peaceful, reflective end to the hiking experiences of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to departure airport — Christchurch (approximately 3.5 hours from Picton via SH1) or return to Queenstown (approximately 5.5 hours). Allow ample time for the journey and check-in. If flying from Christchurch, a brief stop at the Christchurch Botanic Gardens or the Canterbury Museum is worthwhile if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final night in New Zealand. If an overnight stay is needed before a morning flight, check in to airport accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Final New Zealand breakfast — treat yourself to a proper brunch at a Picton café such as Le Café or Seumas' before hitting the road.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route — Kaikōura (if passing through) for a final crayfish snack, or a café in Christchurch city center.
meals.dinner: Christchurch — if departing from CHC, try Riverside Market for a final New Zealand food hall experience with craft beer, local produce, and diverse cuisine options. A great send-off meal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and departure airport well in advance. Christchurch International Airport (CHC) is the most common South Island international departure point. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Return rental car with a full tank of petrol. November traffic on SH1 between Picton and Christchurch is generally straightforward. This itinerary covers approximately 1,800–2,000 km of driving across the South Island — fuel costs should be budgeted at approximately NZD $300–400 total for a standard vehicle.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle through the stunning Milford Sound fiord, exploring sea caves, waterfalls, and dramatic coastal cliffs. This guided kayaking experience puts you right at water level with views of Mitre Peak and lush rainforest. Wildlife encounters with dolphins, seals, and penguins are common. Perfect blend of light activity and breathtaking scenery for hikers who love coastal environments.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge on New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Operated by AJ Hackett, the pioneers of commercial bungee jumping, this is a bucket-list adrenaline experience. The gondola ride to the pod over the canyon is thrilling in itself. A must-do for adventure seekers visiting the South Island, conveniently based near Queenstown's lakefront.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Hike a section of the famous Abel Tasman Coast Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, winding through golden-sand beaches, turquoise bays, and native bush. The Torrent Bay to Bark Bay section is particularly stunning with beachfront camping spots and tidal crossings. Water taxis can drop you off and pick you up, making it flexible for day hikers. Combine hiking with swimming in pristine coastal waters.
experiences.location: Abel Tasman National Park, Tasman Bay

experiences.name: Queenstown Waterfront Dining Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a memorable dinner at one of Queenstown's iconic lakefront restaurants such as Rata or Botswana Butchery, showcasing New Zealand's finest local produce including South Island lamb, Central Otago pinot noir, and fresh seafood. Dine with panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. A perfect cultural and culinary reward after days of adventure activities.

experiences.name: Kaikoura Coastal Clifftop Walk & Whale Watch
experiences.description: Combine a scenic clifftop hike along the Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway with a world-class whale watching boat tour. The walkway hugs the dramatic coastline with seals basking on rocks below and views of the Seaward Kaikoura Ranges. The whale watching cruise offers close encounters with sperm whales, dolphins, and albatross. Kaikoura is one of the world's best marine wildlife destinations, blending hiking and ocean culture seamlessly.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Check in, settle into your suite, and enjoy a welcome champagne with panoramic views of the Nevis Valley. Take a leisurely stroll around the property grounds to acclimatize and soak in the dramatic high-country landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Waterfront Dining Experience — head into Queenstown (30-min scenic drive) for a memorable dinner at Rata or Botswana Butchery, two of Queenstown's most celebrated lakefront restaurants. Enjoy locally sourced South Island cuisine paired with premium Central Otago wines.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light grazing platter and welcome drinks at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay upon check-in
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant or Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — fine dining with lakefront views; expect tasting menus featuring venison, lamb, and seasonal South Island produce

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer in advance. Confirm dinner reservation at Rata or Botswana Butchery. Allow time for jet lag recovery — keep the evening relaxed after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — the headline adventure experience. Transfer to the AJ Hackett Nevis Bungy platform, perched 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This is New Zealand's highest bungy jump, offering 8.5 seconds of freefall with breathtaking high-country views. Book the VIP experience for private cabin access and professional photography package.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay for a recovery lunch and a guided property walk or horse trekking session through the golden tussock hills of the Nevis Valley — a quintessential high-country New Zealand experience available through the property.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the boutique stay. Enjoy a private chef-prepared dinner at the lodge featuring Central Otago lamb, local cheeses, and Pinot Noir from the nearby Gibbston Valley wine region. Unwind in the outdoor hot tub under a spectacular starlit sky.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — eggs Benedict, fresh-baked pastries, local fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Post-bungy recovery lunch at the lodge — hearty antipasto boards, artisan breads, and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — Central Otago lamb rack, roasted root vegetables, and a curated Gibbston Valley Pinot Noir flight

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. Book the VIP photography and video package for lasting memories. Confirm horse trekking with the property concierge the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight from Queenstown over The Remarkables mountain range and Fiordland — a premium add-on offering unrivalled aerial perspectives of South Island's most dramatic landscapes. Land on a remote alpine snowfield for a champagne toast before returning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gibbston Valley Wine Trail — private chauffeured wine tour through the Gibbston Valley, known as the 'Valley of the Vines.' Visit two or three boutique wineries including Amisfield or Gibbston Valley Winery for exclusive cellar-door tastings and a behind-the-scenes winery cave tour.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro — one of New Zealand's most celebrated wine-country restaurants. The 'Trust the Chef' menu pairs seasonal dishes with Amisfield's estate wines in a stunning lakeside setting.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay
meals.lunch: Winery platter lunch at Gibbston Valley Winery — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and estate Pinot Noir in the historic wine cave
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — Trust the Chef tasting menu with wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter experience and Amisfield dinner well in advance — both are extremely popular in the November summer season. Arrange private chauffeur for the wine tour to ensure safe and comfortable travel.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or private transfer to Queenstown (approx. 30 minutes). Explore the Queenstown Hill Time Walk — a rewarding 2-hour return hike offering 360-degree panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. A perfect moderate hike to begin building trail legs for the days ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown Luge and Gondola experience at Bob's Peak — ride the Skyline Gondola to the summit for sweeping views, followed by a luge run down the mountain. Alternatively, explore Queenstown's boutique shopping precinct along the lakefront for premium New Zealand souvenirs, merino wool, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Waterfront Dining Experience — if not visited on Day 1, this is the ideal evening. Dine at Botswana Butchery for a premium steakhouse experience with South Island grass-fed beef, or try Fishbone Bar & Grill for outstanding fresh seafood with lake views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay before departing
meals.lunch: Casual lakefront lunch at Queenstown's Yonder or Bespoke Kitchen — fresh, locally sourced café-style dining
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery or Fishbone Bar & Grill, Queenstown — premium lakefront fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy trail shoes for the Queenstown Hill hike. The summit views are best in the morning before afternoon clouds roll in. Allow extra time in Queenstown town centre if shopping is of interest.

day_by_day.morning: Early private transfer to Milford Sound (approx. 4-hour scenic drive via the Milford Road — one of the world's great alpine drives). Stop at Mirror Lakes, The Divide, and Homer Tunnel for photographs along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking — paddle through the stunning fiord exploring sea caves, cascading waterfalls including Lady Bowen Falls, and the dramatic Mitre Peak coastline. Opt for a private guided kayak tour for an exclusive, unhurried experience. Spot fur seals, dolphins, and rare Fiordland penguins.
day_by_day.evening: Return scenic drive toward Te Anau. Check in at a luxury lodge in Te Anau — recommended: Fiordland Lodge, offering stunning lake views and premium accommodation. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the lodge restaurant overlooking Lake Te Anau.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay for the road journey
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the kayak — your guide will provide a premium packed lunch eaten on the water or at a scenic rest point
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge Restaurant, Te Anau — locally sourced venison, lamb, and fresh fish with South Island wine selection

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — depart by 7:00am to arrive at Milford Sound in time for the afternoon kayak. Book the private kayak tour well in advance as Milford Sound experiences are heavily subscribed in November. Overnight in Te Anau rather than returning to Nevis Valley to reduce driving fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Luxury Cruise — return to Milford Sound for a morning premium small-group or private vessel cruise. Glide beneath Stirling Falls, observe the sheer 1,200-meter cliff faces, and enjoy onboard commentary from an expert naturalist guide. Premium vessels offer gourmet canapés and local wine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown, stopping at Lake Marian Track near Hollyford Valley — a stunning 3-hour return hike through ancient beech forest to an alpine lake surrounded by dramatic peaks. A moderately challenging hike with extraordinary reward.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Enjoy a quiet evening with a private chef dinner at the lodge, reflecting on two days of Fiordland's extraordinary wilderness.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Fiordland Lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet canapés and wine onboard the Milford Sound luxury cruise
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — roasted South Island salmon, seasonal greens, and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Book the private or small-group Milford Sound cruise separately from the kayak experience. The Lake Marian Track can be muddy — waterproof hiking boots are essential. Allow 5–6 hours driving total today including the hike stop.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast, and take advantage of any in-house spa or wellness facilities. A guided meditation or yoga session in the tussock hills can be arranged through the property concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nevis Valley on mountain bikes — arrange premium e-bike hire through the property for a guided ride along high-country trails with views across the valley. Alternatively, enjoy fly fishing on the Nevis River, a world-class trout fishing destination, with a private licensed guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge terrace with a curated cheese and charcuterie board, followed by a private chef-prepared dinner celebrating the midpoint of your journey — a special degustation menu with Central Otago wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the lodge — eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh fruit platters, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light picnic lunch on the trail or riverbank — arranged by the lodge concierge
meals.dinner: Special degustation dinner at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — 5-course private chef menu with Central Otago Pinot Noir and Riesling pairings

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate recovery day after two intensive Fiordland days. Fly fishing requires a New Zealand sports fishing licence — the lodge concierge can arrange this in advance. Confirm e-bike or fishing activity preference the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Wanaka (approx. 1 hour from Queenstown). Visit the iconic Roys Peak Track — one of New Zealand's most photographed hikes. The 16km return trail climbs 1,279 meters to the summit ridge above Lake Wanaka with jaw-dropping views of Mount Aspiring National Park. An early start is essential.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Roys Peak and explore Wanaka township. Visit the Wanaka Tree — the famous lone willow growing in Lake Wanaka — and browse Wanaka's boutique galleries and artisan stores. Enjoy a lakeside coffee at Francesca's Italian Kitchen or Kika.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Wanaka at Francesca's Italian Kitchen — a beloved fine-dining institution celebrated for house-made pasta, wood-fired dishes, and an exceptional wine list. Return to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the lodge before 6:00am departure for Roys Peak
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at Kika Wanaka — seasonal small plates, wood-fired flatbreads, and natural wines in a relaxed lakeside setting
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — house-made pasta, premium South Island ingredients, and Italian-inspired fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is a strenuous hike — start no later than 6:30am to avoid afternoon heat and crowds. Carry 2–3 litres of water and high-energy snacks. The summit can be windy even in November — bring a windproof layer. Book Francesca's well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Skydive Queenstown — for the ultimate adrenaline experience to complement the Nevis Bungy. A tandem skydive from 15,000 feet above Queenstown offers 60 seconds of freefall over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables. Book the premium package with professional video and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown Jet Boat experience on the Shotover River — the iconic Shotover Jet navigates the narrow Shotover Canyon at high speed, combining breathtaking scenery with precision 360-degree spins. A quintessential Queenstown adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening back at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Outdoor hot tub session under the stars, followed by a light private dinner at the lodge — charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and a bottle of reserve Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay
meals.lunch: Post-adventure lunch at Fergburger (iconic Queenstown institution) or a sit-down meal at The Bunker — Queenstown's intimate fine-dining retreat
meals.dinner: Light private dinner at the lodge — premium cheese board, charcuterie, sourdough, and Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Skydiving requires booking well in advance — November is peak season. Weather-dependent activity; have a flexible backup plan. Minimum age 16, maximum weight 100kg for tandem skydive. Shotover Jet runs year-round and can usually be booked same-day, but advance booking is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike on the Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown — a challenging full-day summit hike (5–7 hours return) rising to 1,748 meters with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and the surrounding ranges. Take the Skyline Gondola to the trailhead for an efficient start.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond summit hike — the upper ridge trail is exposed and exhilarating, rewarding hikers with one of the finest 360-degree views in the South Island. Descend via the same route or the longer Tiki Trail back to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at Queenstown's finest — Rata Restaurant by chef Josh Emett. Enjoy a creative tasting menu showcasing the best of New Zealand's seasonal produce, paired with an exceptional wine list in an elegant heritage building setting.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the lodge before an early Queenstown departure
meals.lunch: Summit picnic lunch — premium packed lunch prepared by the lodge including sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and a thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — chef Josh Emett's signature tasting menu with New Zealand wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a serious alpine hike — hire a private guide for safety and enhanced experience. Carry warm layers, rain gear, and at least 2 litres of water. The summit can have snow in November — check conditions with the guide beforehand. Book Rata well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Kaikoura Coastal Clifftop Walk & Whale Watch — depart early by private transfer or domestic flight to Kaikoura (approx. 5-hour drive or 1-hour flight from Queenstown). Begin the Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway, a stunning 3-hour coastal clifftop hike with views of seal colonies, dramatic ocean scenery, and the Kaikoura Ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaikoura Whale Watch — join the world-renowned Whale Watch Kaikoura boat tour. Kaikoura's unique deep-water canyon makes it one of the best places on Earth to see sperm whales year-round. November also brings migrating humpback whales and dusky dolphins. Book the premium small-group tour.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Kaikoura at The Pier Hotel or Hislops Wholefoods Café — celebrate the day's extraordinary wildlife encounters with fresh Kaikoura crayfish (the town's signature seafood), locally caught fish, and craft New Zealand beer or Marlborough wine. Overnight in Kaikoura at a premium lodge such as Kaikoura Boutique Hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay before departure, or airport lounge if flying
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed on the clifftop walkway with ocean views
meals.dinner: The Pier Hotel or dedicated seafood restaurant in Kaikoura — fresh crayfish, grilled fish, and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: This is a significant travel day. Flying Queenstown–Christchurch–Kaikoura is recommended over driving for time efficiency. Book Whale Watch Kaikoura well in advance — tours fill up months ahead in peak season. Whale watching is weather and sea-condition dependent; have a contingency plan.

day_by_day.morning: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike — transfer north to the Abel Tasman National Park (approx. 3-hour drive from Kaikoura or water taxi from Marahau). Hike a premium section of the famous Abel Tasman Coast Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks. The golden-sand beaches, turquoise bays, and lush coastal forest make this one of the world's most beautiful coastal walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Abel Tasman hike through Anchorage Bay and Torrent Bay, with optional water taxi pickup to explore the coastline by boat. Spot New Zealand fur seals, shorebirds, and the remarkably clear Abel Tasman waters. Arrive at Marahau or Kaiteriteri for afternoon refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Nelson or Motueka for the night — check in at a premium Nelson accommodation such as The Honest Lawyer Country Hotel or a luxury lodge. Dinner at Hopgoods & Co in Nelson — one of the South Island's most acclaimed restaurants, celebrated for its seasonal, locally sourced menu and outstanding wine list.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the Kaikoura boutique hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic lunch on Anchorage Bay — premium packed lunch with local cheeses, artisan bread, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Hopgoods & Co, Nelson — seasonal tasting menu with Marlborough and Nelson wine pairings
